environment.description: Celery worker running in Podman container on RHEL 9 host with SELinux enforcing. Container is assigned SELinux type 'celeryworker_t' via a custom policy module (celeryworker.pp) compiled from celeryworker.te. The policy module defines type transitions and confines the process domain. The policy includes: (1) dontaudit rules suppressing AVC denials for /proc and /sys reads, (2) allow rules for network connect to Redis port 6379 only, (3) file context labels restrict write access to paths matching /var/spool/logworker(/.*)?  with type celeryworker_data_t, (4) the process domain celeryworker_t has 'mlsprocwrite' capability removed via a boolean (celeryworker_restrict_resources=on) which triggers the kernel cgroup controller integration denying CPU time beyond 50ms per scheduling period via cpu.cfs_quota_us when the boolean is active. Worker concurrency is set to prefork with 1 process. The net effect is that any single task regex evaluation that exceeds ~50ms of continuous CPU is preempted by the kernel scheduler and the process receives SIGXCPU, causing the Celery worker to terminate the task with a TimeLimitExceeded exception.
